a.epitaph: The fed's own rule, stated on the page itself: inductees must be officially retired five months and receive a three-quarters vote from the CHZ staff. Five inductions survive in the held record, all from the promotion's first year and a half — Millenium (its first champion), Kryptosonic (its only undefeated titleholder), the tag team Sex and Violence and Jaguar-F (both 14 March 2000), and Rufus Blaq, its first two-time World Champion. Nothing held documents any induction after November 2000.

a.name: Joe Smallze Memorial Cup
a.epitaph: A cup FAW gave in memory of Joe “Soulja” Smallze, who wrestled here and died in April 2002. One holder survives in the record: Tony Vigilante, introduced on the 10 August 2003 Panic as “the Joe Smallze 2003 memorial cup holder”. Nothing else in the surviving record describes how it was contested or who else ever held it. It is the second thing FAW named for him — the fed retired its Television Championship unfilled in his name the year before.
a.author: ai
a.source: FAW's own Panic recap of 10 August 2003 (promotions/faw/archive/panic-2003-08-10.html) — the ring announcer's own introduction: “he is the Joe Smallze 2003 memorial cup holder and number one contender to the FAW World Heavyweight Championship... Mr. Tony Vigilante!!!” A second source, nine days earlier: FAW’s own Panic preview of 1 August 2003, carried on eWNews (promotions/ew-news-2002/news/panic-preview-08-03-2003-2003-08-01.html), names the runner-up — Spawn, “more than displeased since losing the Joe Smallze Memorial Cup to Tony Vigilante in the Final.”

a.name: Match of the Year
a.vote_detail: 31%, the World Title Cage Match — a three-way tie for third at 23% each (Studog Escobar, Twiztid, the Dark Lords, Team Esco, Nephilim, Ace Thunder); no second place recorded in the ceremony's own recap table. The ceremony's own script names the match "the World Title Cage Match at Fear the Raine"; the following year's ceremony instead calls the same pairing's win a match "at March Maelstrom II" — the two GIWF ceremony scripts disagree with each other on the event name, not just with any outside source; recorded as an open discrepancy between two primary documents rather than silently resolved. CORRECTED from an earlier registry entry that credited the-phenomenons here, sourced only from a later, self-attested Hall of Fame induction boast. The actual GIWF ceremony transcript — a live, contemporary primary source — settles it: the Phenomenons placed in that three-way tie for third at 23%, not first. See giwf-2000-match-of-the-year's own provenance note for where the Phenomenons' real Match of the Year win actually landed. | 47.06%, Venetian Home Rumble I — the Phenomenons vs. Al Crud & the joke gimmick Tom the Christmas Tree, fought at Christmas Clash '99 — over Slasher/CA$H's THC Title War (23.53%), the Nightmare Reflections Match (17.65%), and Al Crud/Pete Steele's Regal Rumble main event (11.76%). PROVENANCE NOTE, resolving a dating discrepancy: a Phenomenons Hall of Fame induction speech elsewhere self-attests a "1999 GIWF Match of the Year" win for this same Venetian Home Rumble; the actual match happened at a Dec 1999 show, but the GIWF's own annual-awards cycle crowned it at the ceremony covering "year 2000" (the 1999 ceremony's own Match of the Year, held only weeks earlier, had already gone to Curt Raines & Hamish McGrubber — see giwf-1999-match-of-the-year). Read together, the two contemporary ceremony transcripts show the HOF speech's own claim as misdated by one ceremony cycle, not fabricated: right match, wrong year named. Both rows stand, each receipted to its own ceremony's own primary transcript. Independently corroborated by a later UWF retrospective ("the battle... that had won the 2000 Match of the Year award") and a Christmas Clash 2000 preview calling Rumble I the favorite for the award.
a.source: promotions/giwf/archive/giwf-1999-in-character-awards-ceremony.html | promotions/giwf/archive/giwf-2000-in-character-awards-ceremony.html; promotions/uwf/archive/contest-of-champions-2002.html; promotions/giwf/archive/christmas-clash-2000.html

a.name: Wrestler of the Year
a.vote_detail: Shared. Seymour Almasy and Saij tied on 13 votes each of the 43 cast, and were declared co-holders of the award. Argyle took nominations by private message through November 2004 ("Character, not handler"; one to three picks, each with reasons), short-listed the five characters nominated more than once, and counted a private ballot sent to him by private message. Third was AWS Man (also known as Bill), then Jason Hughes, then Chris Storm. Each winner was promised a splash image in the site's random rotation. | Chosen from 21 self-nominated characters by a ballot sent privately to Argyle, each vote required to give reasons including at least one feat the nominee had not listed; voting closed at midnight on 31 December 2005. Deville put his own case forward on the forum's 2005 nomination thread on 9 December 2005, and the result was billed for PTC Radio's first 2006 edition, in mid-January 2006. Fellow nominee Rich Rollins campaigned for the award in character with a hype video, posted on 30 December 2005 and re-uploaded to YouTube in 2007 as "PTC WOTY 2005 Rollins"; its claim of the award for Rollins is his own campaign's, and the ballot went to Deville. | The first PTC Wrestler of the Year, decided by members' vote in the 2003 PTC Awards; by her own count, she took 11 votes, one more than double the runner-up's. The award earned her a splash image in the site's random rotation. | No official award. Self-nominations opened on 16 February 2007 and closed at the end of that month; Argyle later wrote that there was no official 2006 Wrestler of the Year because the nominations were too few and too thin, and that Doctor Curiosity's handler "ended up awarding it to himself". Doctor Curiosity crowned himself PTC Wrestler of the Year 2006 in character on 2 May 2007, and PTCpedia carries him as the unofficial winner. Tchu disputed the claim in character in December 2007. | Nominations by private message to Argyle opened on 2 December 2007. No winner was declared: PTCpedia, captured in March 2008, gives 2007 as "To be determined". Clinton Sage's own handler posted on 28 March 2008 that Clinton Sage and Jason Snow "swept the votes", and in May 2008 that the two had "'unofficially' tied" for the award; that claim is his own.
a.source: PTC forum, Announcements: "Winner - Ptc Wrestler Of The Year..." a.epitaph: The rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own cruiserweight companion to the year-end 200, run alongside the ballot's growing name through the spring and summer of 1998 (a Top 50, then a Top 75, before the results finally posted as a Top 100) and printed as a countdown with a written entry for most of the field.

a.name: Top 200
a.epitaph: The rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll, counted every January and posted back to the group: two hundred wrestlers placed in order, with a written entry for the top twenty-five in most years. Eight editions survive, ranking 1996 through 2004, and the compiler of the first two cross-referenced them himself — the 1997 edition names a wrestler's 1996 place thirty-two times, twice getting the number wrong. What the poll is worth now is not the order it put people in but the census it took by accident: 1,610 placings, and in every year but the first, each one tagged with the federation the wrestler was writing for.
a.author: ai

a.name: Top 10 Rankings
a.epitaph: WIA’s own staff ranked its top ten wrestlers with a paragraph of commentary apiece — praising roleplays, noting who’d stepped up and who was still waiting to debut. One clean edition survives whole, dated January 2003. A second, undated Top 10 sidebar survives on the fed’s own later news/front page (Wayback-captured 26 March 2003, bounded no earlier than 20 January 2003): eight names carry over, Spastic and AAH drop out, and David Valdez and Hunter Tazi appear for the first time — consistent with Spastic’s own move from wrestler to owner on 26 January — but nothing dates that second list precisely enough to ledger it as its own year-bestowal alongside the first, so it stands as prose here rather than a second row.
